Align.description:
Put every stream on one regular time grid.

Each grid point takes the stream's sample at exactly that time if there is
one, even if that sample is missing. (Rows flagged ``NO_SAMPLE``, which a join
of several inputs adds, aren't samples.) Otherwise it takes a value from nearby
valid samples, chosen by ``method``, and is flagged ``RESAMPLED``. With no
valid sample within ``tolerance``, the point is NaN and flagged ``MISSING``.
The grid is anchored at multiples of ``freq`` from the Unix epoch, so the
same data always gives the same grid.

how.description: outer: the grid spans every stream's data; inner: only the time all streams cover.
how.title: How

method.description: nearest: the closest valid sample; previous: the last valid sample at or before the grid time; linear: time-weighted between the valid samples either side.
method.title: Method

name.description: Optional label for this step, shown in provenance and reports. Must be unique within a spec.
name.title: Name

tolerance.description: nearest/previous: how far away a sample may be (default: freq). linear: the largest allowed gap between the two samples either side (default: 2 x freq).
tolerance.title: Tolerance

Align.title: Align

Combine.description:
Build a new stream from several, e.g. two redundant meters.

The result is flagged ``DERIVED``. For ``coalesce``, each sample takes the
first stream (in order) that has a value, along with that stream's flags. For
the other methods, the result's flags are the OR of every input's flags.

how.description: How to combine the values at each time.
how.title: How

name.description: Optional label for this step, shown in provenance and reports. Must be unique within a spec.
name.title: Name

units.description: Units of the result. Required if the inputs' units differ; defaults to their common units.
units.title: Units

Combine.title: Combine

Reject values wherever a user-written condition holds.

For example ``invalid_when="pressure < 0 or pump_on == 0"``. Flags the
rejected values with ``flag``, ``MANUAL`` by default.

Hampel.description:
Reject spikes with a Hampel filter: a rolling median plus a robust spread.

Each value is compared with the median of a centred time window. It is
flagged ``OUTLIER`` if it lies more than ``n_sigma`` robust standard deviations
from that median. The robust standard deviation is
1.4826 × the window's median absolute deviation; 1.4826 is the fixed factor
that makes this match the standard deviation for normal data, so ``n_sigma``
is the only threshold to tune. See Pearson, R. K. (2002),
"Outliers in process modeling and identification", IEEE Trans. Control
Systems Technology 10(1), 55-63, doi:10.1109/87.974338.

The window should be several times wider than the spikes being removed, and
narrow enough that the signal's own trend changes little across it.

A spread estimated from a short window can come out much smaller than the
real noise, and then ordinary noise gets flagged. This happens most where
the signal is flat. Set ``min_scale`` to the sensor's noise standard
deviation, or its resolution, to put a floor under the spread.

min_periods.description: Fewest valid samples a window needs before it can flag.
min_periods.title: Min Periods

min_scale.description: Floor on the robust standard deviation, in the stream's units; typically the sensor's noise level.
min_scale.title: Min Scale

n_sigma.description: How many robust standard deviations count as an outlier.
n_sigma.title: N Sigma

name.description: Optional label for this step, shown in provenance and reports. Must be unique within a spec.
name.title: Name

streams.description: The streams this step acts on.
streams.title: Streams

window.description: Width of the centred window, e.g. 1h.
window.title: Window

Hampel.title: Hampel

Interpolate.description:
Fill short interior gaps by interpolating between the valid values either side.

A gap is a run of missing values. Its length is the time between the valid
sample before it and the valid sample after it. Only gaps no longer than
``max_gap`` are filled: on 5-minute data, ``max_gap="15min"`` fills up to two
missing samples in a row. Gaps at the start or end of the data, and values
flagged ``EXCLUDED`` or ``NO_SAMPLE``, are never filled. Filled values keep
the flags that explain why they were missing, and gain ``IMPUTED_SHORT``.

Methods use numpy and scipy:

- ``linear``: :func:`numpy.interp`;
- ``nearest`` and ``previous``: :class:`scipy.interpolate.interp1d`;
- ``pchip``: :class:`scipy.interpolate.PchipInterpolator`, shape-preserving
  with no overshoot;
- ``akima``: :class:`scipy.interpolate.Akima1DInterpolator`.

max_gap.description: Longest gap to fill, measured between the valid samples either side, e.g. 15min.
max_gap.title: Max Gap

name.description: Optional label for this step, shown in provenance and reports. Must be unique within a spec.
name.title: Name

streams.description: The streams this step acts on.
streams.title: Streams

Interpolate.title: Interpolate

Mask.description:
Keep data only where a condition holds; exclude the rest.

Use this to select operating periods, e.g. ``keep_when="pump_on == 1"``.
Excluded values become NaN and are flagged ``EXCLUDED``, which marks them as
deliberately left out, not as bad data. Imputers never fill them. With
``drop_rows``, the rows are removed instead.

drop_rows.description: Remove rows where the condition fails, instead of excluding values.
drop_rows.title: Drop Rows

keep_when.description: Condition over stream names, e.g. 'pump_on == 1 and flow > 0'.
keep_when.title: Keep When

name.title: Name

streams.description: Streams to exclude values from (default: all).
streams.title: Streams

RateOfChange.description:
Reject values that change faster than the process physically can.

Each value is compared with the last *accepted* value. If
``|change| / elapsed time`` exceeds ``max_rate`` per ``per``, the value is
flagged ``RATE_OF_CHANGE``. A spike is caught without flagging the point
after it, because that point is compared with the last good value before the
spike. A genuine step change is accepted once enough time has passed for the
allowed rate to cover it.

name.title: Name

per.description: Time unit of max_rate, e.g. 1h or 1min.
per.title: Per

streams.description: The streams this step acts on.
streams.title: Streams

Resample.description:
Aggregate every stream into fixed time bins.

Bins are left-closed and labelled by their start, and anchored at multiples of
``freq`` from the Unix epoch. A bin's flags are the OR of its samples' flags,
plus ``RESAMPLED`` when it has a value. A bin with no samples at all is
flagged ``MISSING``.

agg.description: How to aggregate the valid samples in a bin.
agg.title: Agg

min_count.description: Fewest valid samples a bin needs to get a value.
min_count.title: Min Count

name.description: Optional label for this step, shown in provenance and reports. Must be unique within a spec.
name.title: Name

Shift.description:
Shift streams in time, e.g. to undo a known transport delay.

A positive ``by`` moves values later. It needs a regular index, and ``by``
must be a whole number of steps. Grid points left without a value are
flagged ``MISSING``.

by.description: How far to move the values, e.g. 5min or -5min.
by.title: By

name.description: Optional label for this step, shown in provenance and reports. Must be unique within a spec.
name.title: Name

streams.description: The streams this step acts on.
streams.title: Streams

Shift.title: Shift

Stuck.description:
Reject flat-lined runs, the signature of a frozen sensor or a held last value.

A run is consecutive valid samples whose values differ by at most
``tolerance``. Missing samples in between don't break a run. Every sample of
a run lasting ``min_duration`` or longer is flagged ``STUCK``. Runs at a value
listed in ``exclude_values`` are left alone; this is useful for a legitimate
constant such as 0 when a pump is off.

exclude_values.description: Values at which a flat run is legitimate, e.g. [0].
exclude_values.title: Exclude Values

min_duration.description: Shortest flat run that counts as stuck, e.g. 1h.
min_duration.title: Min Duration

name.description: Optional label for this step, shown in provenance and reports. Must be unique within a spec.
name.title: Name

streams.description: The streams this step acts on.
streams.title: Streams

tolerance.description: Largest change between samples that still counts as flat.
tolerance.title: Tolerance

Stuck.title: Stuck

Tukey.description:
Reject values beyond Tukey's fences, learned from the training data.

``fit`` records each stream's quartiles Q1 and Q3. Values below
``Q1 - k·IQR`` or above ``Q3 + k·IQR`` are flagged ``OUTLIER``, where
IQR = Q3 - Q1. Use k = 1.5 for "outliers" and k = 3 for "far out" values
(Tukey, J. W. (1977), *Exploratory Data Analysis*, Addison-Wesley).

This suits streams whose normal range doesn't drift. For a signal with a
strong trend or regimes, prefer ``hampel``.

k.description: Fence width in multiples of the IQR.
k.title: K

name.description: Optional label for this step, shown in provenance and reports. Must be unique within a spec.
name.title: Name

streams.description: The streams this step acts on.
streams.title: Streams

Tukey.title: Tukey

description:
A declarative, versioned description of a pipeline.

``steps`` accepts step objects or plain dicts with a ``kind``. Dicts are
resolved through the step registry. :func:`flexsignal.spec.load_spec` is the
preferred way to read a spec from JSON, because its errors point at the exact
field.
